precepts.text: The same command word for word: pure oil olive beaten for the light, the lamps ordered from evening unto morning before the Lord continually, a statute for ever.
precepts.point: Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Brotherhood and unity, and correction, which is an excellent oil that shall not break the head, are that oil; if you are not around a body being built up and corrected by teachers and peers, that is how people run out of oil, their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, offered as a meditation.

note.label: Exodus 27: The Altar, the Court, and the Oil for the Lamp

precepts.why:
Leviticus gives the same command word for word: “Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Without the vail of the testimony, in the tabernacle of the congregation, shall Aaron order it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually: it shall be a statute for ever in your generations. He shall order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.”

The children of Israel bring the oil; Aaron and his sons order the lamps from evening to morning before the Lord; and the lamp burns always, a statute for ever unto their generations.

Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood. So think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life.

precepts.text: The pure candlestick with all his furniture was part of the tabernacle work; the lamps ordered on it burned before the Lord continually.
precepts.point: The children of Israel were commanded to bring pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Aaron ordered it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually, upon the pure candlestick, a statute for ever in your generations.

note.label: Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer

precepts.why:
The children of Israel were commanded to bring “pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually”, and Aaron was to “order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.”

That pure candlestick was part of the tabernacle work: “the table and his furniture, and the pure candlestick with all his furniture, and the altar of incense.” The lamps Aaron ordered from the evening unto the morning burned upon it before the Lord continually, a statute for ever in your generations.

precepts.text: Ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye; but I say unto you that ye resist not evil; Christ magnified the law for how brothers deal with brothers.
precepts.point: Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience, and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that.

note.label: Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer

precepts.why:
“Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be done to him again.” When Christ came he taught the proper understanding of eye for eye for dealing inside the nation: “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil.”

As the Son of God he had authority to magnify the law: “whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.”

Inside our nation we must practice forgiveness, patience and long-suffering; we are dealing with our own people, brothers with a conscience. We are the most forgiving people on the planet; the only time we do not know how to forgive is when it comes to each other, and Christ dealt with that here.

precepts.text: The oil for the lamps and the showbread were commanded to be kept continually, an everlasting statute the fathers had abandoned.
precepts.point: He names the sin plainly: the fathers had trespassed, forsaken the Most High, turned their backs on his habitation, shut the doors, put out the lamps, and stopped burning incense and offering burnt offerings.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The Most High commanded “pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually”, “a statute for ever in your generations.” Aaron was to “order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.” The twelve cakes of the showbread were set “in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord”, with “pure frankincense upon each row”, and “Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the Lord continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.”

The oil for the lamps and the showbread were to be kept continually, an everlasting statute, and the fathers abandoned it. Hezekiah names the sin plainly: “they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the God of Israel.” They “have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord, and turned their backs.”

So Hezekiah, who “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done”, went straight to it: “in the first year of his reign, in the first month”, he “opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them”, and charged the Levites, “sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.”

points: The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, strove with a man of Israel in the camp, and the Israelitish woman's son blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. We came out of Egypt, and some of our sisters had children by the Egyptians; his mother was Shelomith, a Danite sister.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: When it says he cursed, it does not mean modern curse words; it means he spoke ill of the Lord. Blaspheming and cursing here are the same thing: insulting the divine.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: They put him in ward, meaning they locked him up, that the mind of the Lord might be shewed them. And the Lord said, bring forth him that hath cursed without the camp, and let all the congregation stone him. Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin, and he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. Under Moses, blaspheming the Lord was an immediate death sentence, for the stranger as well as for him born in the land.

note.label: Leviticus 24: The Pure Oil, the Shewbread, and the Blasphemer

points: The son of an Israelitish woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel, and strove in the camp with a man of Israel, and blasphemed the name of the Lord, and cursed. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

His father being an Egyptian shows he was conceived while Israel was in captivity in the land of Egypt, dwelling among the Egyptians; in the same way Moses, outside of Egypt with Jethro the priest of Midian, took a wife there. And there is no such thing as being half Israelite or a fourth Israelite: if your parent is Israel, you are Israel.
